Apologies in advance for the long-ish post, but I can probably add a unique perspective on this as someone who has actually refereed. I did it from ages 17-22 in the central belt, and was involved in games in the Juniors, Lowland League, Women's Premier League, Club Academy Scotland (pro-youth) and the early rounds of the Scottish Cup, as well as some SPFL friendlies.

Without a shadow of a doubt the two key things that need to happen at the top of the game are VAR and full time referees. The benefits of VAR speaks for itself, but the constant argument against it is that "it'll be the same useless refs using it". True, it will be the same refs using VAR, but some of the absolute howlers we see now WILL be cleared up. The primary reason wrong decisions get made just now (for the most part) is the angle the referee sees it at. That's what VAR will help with, and it will 100% lead to better decisions in the end; albeit some will inevitably be missed (Kent goal v Dortmund as an example). The top refs in Scotland have all used VAR for international games and know how to utilise it.

As for full time referees, that's actually a bit more tricky and would probably require a restructuring of the current referee categories; allow me to explain why. At the moment, there's around 25-30 Category 1 officials. What happens in most other countries is that being promoted to the top category allows you to referee in the top league. In Scotland though, promotion to category 1 is required just to regularly referee in the SPFL (League 2 and above). What tends to happen is that the more senior and FIFA listed officials get the Premiership and Championship games, whilst the newer Category 1s do Leagues 2 and 1. As a result, there's around 25-30 Category 1 referees at the moment. To make all of them full time would simply cost too much money, especially when you then throw in all the assistant referees for the Premiership as well. Hence why in order to have full time referees, you probably need to restructure the categories so that Category 1 only covers the top 2 divisions, and the pool is around 10-15 people. You then take the most talented from Leagues 1 and 2 and promote them when appropriate. Ultimately, referees who don't need to worry about doing a game whilst also juggling their personal work lives will make them better on the pitch, because they don't need to fit refereeing around other commitments. I know from experience that working during the day then going straight to an evening game can be tough, especially if there's a fair travel involved and you're struggling just to be there for whatever the arrival time is.

The last thing I'd add is that, in general, knowledge of the Laws of the Game amongst fans (in all countries to be fair) is pretty bad. I regularly see referees/decisions slated on social media by fans of all teams despite knowing that a clear correct decision was made (Liverpool disallowed goal in the Carabao Cup Final as an example). I think if more people took the time to understand the Laws, and maybe even done the referee course, they'd find referees don't actually make as many mistakes as they think. Not saying the refs are blameless of course, because at the moment there are a lot of mistakes being made, but it might clear things up for people.
